description: Changes in Ding 0.0.9: trusted Types and Vue fixes.
body:
Title transitions work under Trusted Types

When a new toast replaces a visible one, the old title and description animate out under require-trusted-types-for 'script', including when trusted-types 'none' is set. This applies to React, Svelte, Vue and plain DOM. Issue #46

Vue skips equivalent label updates

Passing a new labels object with the same strings no longer reconfigures the Toaster. Changes to either label, position or theme still apply. PR #47

summary: Background countdowns and the Ding skill
description: Changes in Ding 0.0.8: background countdowns and the Ding skill.
body:
Countdowns pause in background tabs

A timed toast shown in the background starts its countdown when you return. If the countdown was already running, it resumes with the time left. This applies to React, Svelte, Vue and plain DOM.

Show the Undo toast, switch to another tab while the line is shrinking, then come back. The line picks up where it left off.

Optional Ding skill for coding agents

The skill covers setup, promises, progress, actions and styling. With Node.js 22.20 or later, run:

npx skills add YusufCeng1z/ding --skill ding

See the manual install and ZIP instructions.

React renderer cleanup

The React renderer is easier to maintain. The existing Next.js setup still mounts Toaster directly in the root layout.

summary: Toast IDs, actions and motion cleanup
description: Changes in Ding 0.0.7: toast IDs, actions and motion cleanup.
body:
Old IDs leave newer messages alone Fixed

toast.dismiss(id) still accepts the ID returned by a toast call, but an older call can no longer dismiss the message that took over its slot. Repeated toasts return a usable caller ID; generated IDs avoid collisions with custom IDs.

Open a loading toast, replace it, then try the old caller ID and the visible item's close control.

Start with Loading.

Async actions close on click Fixed

A synchronous action can still return a patch to morph the toast. An async action starts closing the old toast when clicked; its resolved value is not treated as a patch. Show its result as another toast, or use toast.promise() to morph a loading toast to its result. An action that opens a new toast no longer accidentally closes it.

Drag and animation cleanup Fixed

pointercancel now resets a drag instead of flinging the toast. Unmounting stops its animation work, and two mounted Toasters both receive layout updates in the same frame. Escape and Alt+T keep working when one of two mounted Toasters unmounts, including React.

Upgrading a custom renderer Changed

toast.dismiss(id) and toast.dismiss() remain available. If your custom close button used toast.dismiss(item.id), switch it to toast.close(item.id): the visible item's physical ID may differ from its newest caller ID. The built-in React, Svelte, Vue and plain DOM renderers are already updated. See the API reference. Thanks to Jens for the close(id) distinction and repeat-ID regression.

description: Changes in Ding 0.0.6: held toasts and queue modes.
body:
A toast that waits for you keeps its place Fixed

A toast is held when it stays until dismissed: an error, a toast with a button, or one with duration: 0. Before, any new toast morphed the held one away. Now the held toast stays and quick toasts appear next to it.

Show the error first, then the other two. The error stays.

Choose how toasts share the screen New

The new held option of toast.configure decides what happens when a toast arrives while a held toast is on screen.

toast.configure({ held: 'list' }); // list, queue or replace
  • list is the default. The held toast keeps its place and quick toasts appear next to it. A new held toast takes over the quick one.
  • queue makes new toasts wait in order. They show one after another once the held toast is gone.
  • replace is how 0.0.5 behaved. A new toast morphs the one on screen, held or not.

Pick a mode, then run the three toasts above again.

Upgrading Changed

The default changed from replace to list. If a held toast was replaced before, it now stays until the user dismisses it. To keep the old behavior, set it once:

toast.configure({ held: 'replace' });

In plain DOM, mountToaster({ held: 'replace' }) does the same. A loading toast is not held, because it is about to turn into its result. See Held toasts in the docs.

summary: filled toasts, per-toast styles, custom icons
description: Ding 0.0.5 adds filled toasts, per-toast styles and custom icons. See what changed and how to use each one.
body:
Filled toasts New

Each toast now has three variables you can set per status: --fill for the surface, --on for the text, buttons and focus ring, and --c for the icon. Set them and the whole toast takes the status color. The action button, the second button, the progress bar and the close button follow along.

.tst-viewport .tst[data-type=error] {
  --fill: #dc2626;
  --on: #fff;
  --c: #fff;
}

Colors can use light-dark() to differ per theme. If your site has its own theme switch, pass the theme to Toaster or toast.configure({ theme }).

The same error, plain and filled.

Style one toast New

Pass className and the toast gets that class next to tst. Style it as .tst.your-class. toast.update(id, { className: null }) removes it again.

toast.info('Limited offer', { className: 'gold' });

.tst.gold { --fill: #fff7d6; --on: #5b4200; --c: #c77d00; }

Only the first toast carries the class.

Tune the springs, swap the icons New

toast.configure takes two new options. springs retunes the three motions, enter, morph and stack, with a stiffness and a damping each. Leave one out to keep its default. icons replaces a status icon with your own paths on a 24×24 grid. Both apply to toasts shown afterwards.

toast.configure({
  springs: { enter: { stiffness: 170, damping: 12 } },
  icons: { success: [RING, 'M12 16.4s-3.8-2.3-3.8-5a2.1 2.1 0 0 1 3.8-1.2a2.1 2.1 0 0 1 3.8 1.2c0 2.7-3.8 5-3.8 5z'] },
});

The first path of an icon is its outer ring, which loading toasts draw as a turning arc. Keep three paths for warning and info, because their animations use the second and third.

Each button changes the setting, then shows a toast.

More CSS variables, and a new playground

The docs now list the variables that were already there: --tst-size, --tst-pad, --tst-shadow and --tst-enter-scale, plus the font, which you set on .tst-viewport. The playground was rebuilt around them. Pick a ready-made style, change the radius, size, colors, motion or icon on a real toast, then copy the CSS and config.

See Styling in the docs for the full list.

Square corners work Fixed

--tst-radius: 0 was treated as missing, so toasts stayed rounded at 24px. A radius of 0 now gives square corners. A radius you change while a toast is open also shows up on its next move, where it used to wait for the next toast.

summary: Vue, Next.js without a wrapper, CSP nonce
description: Ding 0.0.4 adds a Vue 3 and Nuxt package, works in Next.js server layouts without a wrapper, supports a CSP nonce, and stops progress toasts from flickering.
body:
Vue 3 and Nuxt New

There is a new package, @yusufceng1z/ding-vue. It has the same props as the React and Svelte ones: position, theme, labels and nonce.

npm i @yusufceng1z/ding-vue
<script setup>
import { Toaster, toast } from '@yusufceng1z/ding-vue';
</script>

<template>
  <Toaster position="top-center" theme="system" />
  <button @click="toast.success('Saved')">Save</button>
</template>

Toaster draws nothing where you put it and starts after the page has loaded, so server rendering is safe. In Nuxt, put it in app.vue and call toast from client code, like a click handler. We ran it in Vue with Vite and in Nuxt 4, in development and in a production build.

Asked for by reslear in issue 7.

Next.js without a wrapper

The React build now starts with "use client". Until now, importing Toaster in a server layout failed, so you needed your own client component around it. You don't any more.

// app/layout.tsx, a server component
import { Toaster } from '@yusufceng1z/ding-react';

export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        <Toaster />
        {children}
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}

Call toast from client components only. See the Next.js guide.

Suggested and built by Amidou Cissé, see pull request 10.

Works with a strict CSP

Ding puts its styles in one <style> element. If your style-src blocks inline styles, give it your page's nonce. Only that element needs it, because the per-toast values are set through the DOM, which CSP allows.

<Toaster nonce={nonce} />     {/* React, Svelte */}
<Toaster :nonce="nonce" />    <!-- Vue -->

mountToaster({ nonce });        // plain DOM

Suggested and built by Amidou Cissé, see pull request 11.

Progress toasts don't flicker Fixed

When a toast changed its own text while it ran, like a download with a moving percentage, the text animation played again on every update and the title looked like it was shaking. Now the animation only plays when the title really becomes something new, such as "Download complete".

Watch the title while the numbers change. It should stay still until the end.

Reported by MathiasWP in issue 5. A screen recording from IsaacHatilima helped find it.

The close button stays last Fixed

In the plain DOM renderer, which Vue and Nuxt use, an error toast has a close button. If it then turned into a toast with an action, like Undo, the close button ended up in front of the action. It now stays at the end. React and Svelte were not affected.

Open the error, then press Undo. The buttons should read Undo, then close.

Buttons: -

For contributors

The React, Svelte, Vue and plain DOM renderers now each have render tests, and CI runs them on every pull request. Thanks to Amidou Cissé for pull request 13 and the three before it.

What's new in 0.0.3

description: Ding 0.0.3 adds localizable labels, bigger buttons and a safer Escape key that yields to dialogs and text fields. What changed and why.
body:
Translate the screen reader labels New

Two names were hard-coded in English: the notifications region and the close button. On a page in another language, a screen reader read the toast in that language and these two controls in English. Now you pass your own strings. Keys you leave out keep the English default.

toast.configure({
  labels: { region: 'Bildirimler', dismiss: 'Bildirimi kapat' },
});

React and Svelte take the same thing as a prop: <Toaster labels={{ dismiss: 'Fermer' }} />. Plain DOM takes it in mountToaster({ labels }).

These names are invisible on the page, only a screen reader says them. Pick a language to see what it would read.

region:  -
close:   -

Suggested and built by Amidou Cissé, see pull request 3.

Bigger click areas

Buttons keep their look but the area that counts as a click grew from 30 to 44 pixels tall, so a thumb that lands slightly above or below still hits. Neighbouring buttons never overlap.

Show the click areas, open the toast, then click just above or below Retry.

No clicks yet

Alt + T reaches every toast

Alt + T moves focus into the toast, which also pauses its timer. Before, it only worked when the toast had a button. A plain "Saved" toast could not be reached by keyboard and disappeared after five seconds. Now focus lands on the toast itself, with a ring inside it.

Open the toast, then press Alt + T within five seconds. It only works in the After mode, because the old code is gone.

Focus: not on a toast

Esc no longer closes toasts behind your back

Esc dismisses toasts, but it used to do that even while you pressed Esc to close a dialog, a menu or to clear a text field. Now it leaves the toast alone when focus is in one of those. Press Esc anywhere else and it still dismisses.

Open a toast that stays. Click into the field or open the dialog, then press Esc.

Toasts on screen: 0

Press Esc. The toast should stay.

Smaller fixes

  • Centered icon. The status icon sat one pixel low next to the text. It is now centered in the pill.
  • Even padding. A toast without buttons had about 29 pixels of space after the text and 12 before the icon. The right side is now about 15, so the pill looks balanced.
  • Safari drag. Dragging a toast no longer highlights its text in Safari.
  • Page styles can't push buttons around. A site-wide button { margin } rule used to shift the close button. The toast now resets its own button margins.

For contributors

A fresh clone now installs, type-checks, tests and builds, and a GitHub Actions workflow runs the same steps on every pull request. Running the tests needs Node 22.18 or newer. The packages themselves still support Node 18 and up. Thanks to Amidou Cissé for pull request 1.

Package setup

Added package READMEs, homepage links and issue tracker URLs. The CommonJS export gained a dedicated type declaration, and the plain DOM toaster can be imported and mounted safely during server rendering.

First public release

Ding shipped its spring-based toast engine with timer, state and plain DOM support, alongside adapters for React and Svelte.

Publishing placeholder

This prerelease was used to stage the npm package before the first public release.
